---
title: "ZenoSolver"
subtitle: "Exact Pareto fronts of MultiZenoTravel planning instances, with certificates and a Lean 4 proof"
toc: false
---

MultiZenoTravel is a bi-objective planning benchmark: $p$ planes carry $t$ passengers from an
initial city $C_I$ to a goal city $C_G$ through $n$ central cities, and every plan has a total
**cost** (landing fees) and a **makespan**. ZenoSolver computes the exact Pareto front of an
instance, so that multi-objective planners can be scored against the true front.

```sh
zeno -n 50 -t 30 -p 5            # 50 central cities, 30 passengers, 5 planes
zeno -n 2 -t 5 -p 2 -d durations-and-costs.dat --certificate front.cert
zeno check front.cert            # verify the certificate without trusting the solver
```

`zeno` prints the front as `cost makespan` lines by increasing cost. It is exact for symmetric
durations, which includes every instance the generator emits. For non-symmetric durations it
prints a certified bracket, and says whether the bracket closes into the exact front.

## How it works

The front is the set of breakpoints of $E(T)$, the least cost of an *admissible* partition of the
$2t-p$ landings into $p$ groups whose durations each sum to at most $T$
([Proposition 7.1](proofs.qmd#node-proposition-7-1)). `zeno` brackets $E$ between a relaxation $L$
and the pairs and chains bounds $U$, $U_3$ on every level, and runs the exact link-forest dynamic
program only where the bracket leaves a level open. The [algorithm page](solver/algorithm.qmd) has
the details, and the [theory note](https://github.com/aquemy/ZenoSolver/blob/master/doc/theory/exact-front.md)
the proofs.

The 2016 ZenoSolver, published with the EvoCOP 2015 paper, scheduled each fixed multiset of
landings greedily, and that greedy is not optimal ([§5](proofs.qmd#node-s5)). The current solver
replaces it and reproduces every golden front of an exhaustive oracle, including those on which the
2016 solvers were wrong.

## What is proved

{{< include _blueprint-stats.md >}}

The front theorem is machine-checked for every instance with symmetric durations and central
flights no faster than through a hub, assumptions (S) and (A1)
([Corollary 4.8](proofs.qmd#node-corollary-4-8)). So are the exactness of both dynamic programs
([Theorem 7.5](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-7-5), [Theorem 7.6](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-7-6)), the
verified solver `zeno-front` ([`solveFront_isParetoFront`](proofs.qmd#node-verified-solver)) and
the soundness of the certificate checker `zeno-check`, symmetric
([Theorem 9.1](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-9-1)) and not
([version 2](proofs.qmd#node-version-2-checker)). For non-symmetric instances the note proves
*schedulable domination* ([Theorem 6.9](proofs.qmd#node-theorem-6-9), machine-checked). The
exhaustive search over role configurations that closes the gaps left by harmful waiting
([Proposition 6.5](proofs.qmd#node-proposition-6-5)) rests on it.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Who did what.** The model and the first algorithms are those of the original papers,
Quemy & Schoenauer (EvoCOP 2015) and Quemy, Schoenauer & Dréo (arXiv:2304.14659, 2023). The
current solver, the theory note that corrects the papers, the Lean 4 formalization and this website
are the work of Alexandre Quemy. On the [blueprint](proofs.qmd), the papers' statements are
reproduced verbatim in grey boxes with their attribution; blue and green boxes hold the note and
the Lean development.
:::
